speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the onset, frequency, and appearance of your diarrhea, and do you have any associated symptoms like fever or abdominal pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent levofloxacin use and symptoms, I am highly suspicious of Clostridioides difficile infection. REQUEST TEST: Stool_toxin_assay_for_C_diff

speaker: Doctor
text: The stool test result for C. difficile toxin is not specified, so we cannot confirm the diagnosis yet. Do you have a fever, and have you noticed any blood or mucus in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Watery diarrhea. I also have Lower abdominal discomfort, Abdominal cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: Your symptoms of watery diarrhea and cramping following levofloxacin use strongly suggest C. difficile infection despite the initial test result. I will order a more sensitive test to confirm this suspicion. REQUEST TEST: C_difficile_Giardia_antigen

speaker: Doctor
text: The C. difficile and Giardia antigen tests are negative, which makes those infections less likely. Do you have any history of inflammatory bowel disease, or have you traveled recently?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Currently being treated for community-acquired pneumonia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, does not consume alcohol. No recent travel or dietary changes reported.

speaker: Doctor
text: With recent antibiotic use and negative initial infectious workup, I need to assess for systemic signs of severe colitis. Have you experienced any high-grade fever, significant nausea, or vomiting, and has your white blood cell count been elevated on recent labs?

speaker: Patient
text: No fever, no recent antibiotics usage apart from levofloxacin for pneumonia, no vomiting, no blood in stool.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of profuse watery diarrhea following levofloxacin therapy is classic for C. difficile infection, even with initial negative toxin assays. I will request a more definitive test to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: C_difficile_toxin_GDHA_EIA

speaker: Doctor
text:
The positive C. difficile toxin GDH EIA confirms the diagnosis of Clostridioides difficile infection. I will now discontinue the levofloxacin and initiate treatment with oral vancomycin.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection
